items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 29, 2026
items.excerpt: Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Thursday, including Israel’s final vote count, renewed efforts to revive US-Iran talks, Spain mourning one of its deadliest train crashes, North Korea’s missile launches, and Flavio Bolsonaro declaring himself Brazil’s “leader” from the US. More than 500,000 outstanding ballots could reshape Israel’s parliamentary seat distribution as counting continues Thursday, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor its main opposition projected to secure a governing majority. Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to win 53 seats, compared with 48 for the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot and a record combined 19 for predominantly Arab parties, according to Channel 12. A majority requires 61 seats in the 120-member Knesset. The outstanding ballots, cast by soldiers and others voting away from their registered polling stations, were expected to be counted by Thursday evening, Israel’s public broadcaster reported. - Trump confirms Vance’s Iran contact as regional powers push for deal President Donald Trump said Washington is communicating with Iran through mediators, as regional governments seek to revive peace negotiations and avert renewed US strikes. The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei at Trump’s direction. Asked about the contact, Trump said he had approved Vance’s request to help Iran obtain medical supplies. “Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” he said. Qatar-led mediators are urging Tehran to allow UN inspectors into bombed nuclear sites in exchange for some US sanctions relief, Axios reported. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Türkiye are supporting the effort. Trump said he did not know whether negotiations would succeed. Trump also had a phone call with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who told him that the Mecca Joint Defense Alliance was closely monitoring developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen. - Spain begins three days of mourning after deadly train crash Spain is in three days of mourning after Wednesday's collision between two high-speed trains killed at least 68 people, one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's recent history. Speaking at the crash site in Toledo, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said authorities would determine the cause of the accident and take action if wrongdoing was uncovered. Sanchez said it was "unacceptable" for a country like Spain to experience two high-speed rail accidents in a single year, referring to January's deadly derailment that claimed the lives of 46 people. "We will get to the bottom of this. If there has been negligence, it will be known," he said, according to Spanish news agency EFE. - Tensions rise as North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles North Korea launched around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, on Thursday, South Korea’s military said. Seoul stepped up surveillance for further launches and shared information with the US and Japan as officials assessed the missiles’ flight distances and other details, Yonhap News reported. Hours earlier, the Japanese Defense Ministry said Pyongyang had fired "what may be a ballistic missile." That prompted a warning from Japan’s Coast Guard urging ships to avoid any fallen objects, Kyodo News reported. - Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself Brazil's leader Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami from Ecuador, despite a court order requiring him to surrender his passports as part of a corruption and money-laundering investigation, according to US media reports. He also published a letter on social media describing himself as the country’s "leader" and vowed to lead the opposition to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva from exile in the US. The son of former President Jair Bolsonaro is under investigation over his alleged links to a banker accused of financial misconduct and a man suspected of money laundering.

items.excerpt: ## Arab Parties Could Determine Next Israeli Prime Minister as Election Produces No Clear Winner Oct 29, 2026 In Israel, Tuesday’s national elections have produced no clear winner, with more than 90% of the votes counted. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party received the most votes, but Netanyahu’s political bloc is likely to fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government. The leading opposition bloc headed by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party is projected to win just 48 seats. Israel’s Arab parties are on track to win an unprecedented 19 seats in the Knesset, driven by a surge in turnout by Palestinian citizens of Israel. They are now in a position to help the opposition form a ruling coalition, but it’s unclear if Eisenkot is open to partnering with Palestinian parties. Netanyahu has accused Arab parties of stealing the election, while providing no evidence. This is the leader of the Palestinian-dominated Joint List, Yousef Jabareen. > Yousef Jabareen: “Our power in the Knesset is very decisive, is very crucial. And as we have promised our community, we would like to use this power to facilitate getting rid of Netanyahu’s government and, hopefully, helping to change the political situation in Israel.”

items.excerpt: Trump lends support for Darline Graham in South Carolina as Republican anxiety rises in Senate race ROCK HILL, S.C. (AP) — President Donald Trump is campaigning in South Carolina as he encourages Republicans to show up for Darline Graham in a critical Senate contest. Graham is trying to fend off a challenge from pediatrician Annie Andrews in a state that hasn't sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly three decades. Andrews is urging voters seeking change to “try something new for once.” Darline Graham was appointed to the Senate in July after the death of her brother Lindsey. She's running for a six-year term. Trump was in Rock Hill on Thursday, where he called Lindsey Graham “a great politician” and said his sister has “the gene.” Trump spent part of his speech opining on other competitive contests, in North Carolina, Michigan, Texas, Minnesota and Alaska. JERUSALEM (AP) — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his party have amplified claims that the country's election was “stolen” by Arab-led parties. Final results are expected to confirm on Thursday that Netanyahu's bloc has lost its majority in parliament. The opposition accuses Netanyahu of demonizing the Arab population after a strong showing by Arab-led parties. If the opposition teams up with those parties in a rare and politically risky move, they could form the next government. The elections committee has asked the Shin Bet intelligence service to investigate alleged election interference by unspecified “foreign entities.” Netanyahu's Likud party targeted Arab-led parties even before the vote, despite lacking specific evidence. WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. economy posted strong growth in the July-September quarter yet inflation remained stubbornly high last month, government reports showed Thursday, painting a mixed picture less than a week before midterm elections in which the uncomfortably high cost of living has become a central issue. Strong consumer spending and soaring investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure were the key drivers of growth in the third quarter. Whenever unemployment is low, like now, consumers often spend at a healthy clip, and wealthier consumers are increasingly spending the fruits of their stock market gains. Yet economists worry that persistently high prices are eroding Americans’ ability to keep spending. WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump says he thinks Alaska’s Democratic U.S. Senate candidate should be “removed from the ballot and prosecuted” over accusations her campaign recruited another candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Trump has cast doubt on whether Democrat Mary Peltola would be seated even if she won the election. The New York Times reports Peltola’s team may have recruited another Dan Sullivan to confuse voters. Trump said Thursday it's “hard to believe” Peltola could even be allowed to run. Alaska Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation, saying tricking voters “strikes at the integrity of our elections.” Peltola dismisses the allegations as a distraction from key issues. ... URDA, Spain (AP) — Spain faces fresh concerns about rail safety after a second high-speed train crash this year killed 69 people. Search teams using sniffer dogs continued to look for victims on Thursday morning a day after the collision in central Spain. One more body was found overnight. The collision Wednesday involved a RENFE train striking a stationary IRYO train in Toledo. This crash comes just weeks before a national election, adding pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government. Spain's transport minister said human error caused the latest crash. Unions pushed back against the minister. Three days of national mourning started Thursday. ... DoorDash is offering $17 billion to buy Instacart to supercharge its grocery delivery business in what would be a big consolidation in grocery delivery. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash.

items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated 3 Hours Ago ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. ... Consu ... There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

Elke Sommer, German-born star of ‘A Shot in the Dark’ and ‘The Prize,’ dies at 85 Elke Sommer, the German actor known for her roles in 1960s Hollywood comedies and espionage films, has died at 85. Her stepson confirmed her passing at her Bel Air home on Wednesday to a German publication. Sommer starred alongside legends like Paul Newman in “The Prize” and Peter Sellers in “A Shot in the Dark.” Born in Berlin during World War II, she was discovered in Italy and quickly rose to fame. Her Hollywood break came with “The Prize,” earning her a Golden Globe. Despite her sex symbol status, Sommer believed her energy, not looks, defined her appeal. ... South Carolina police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after coroner's ruling Police in South Carolina say they have closed their investigation into the overdose death of actor Hayden Panettiere following a coroner’s findings that it was accidental. No charges were filed. Greenville police said Wednesday in a statement the decision was based on the medical examiner’s determination as well as the findings of the investigation. The former star of the TV series “Heroes” and “Nashville” was pronounced dead in an apartment in Greenville on Aug. 16 at age 36 after paramedics found her unresponsive. It remains unclear whether federal agents are still looking into her death separately. A serial killer, an obsessed cop and an undercover FBI agent. Welcome to Apple's 'Nocturne' NEW YORK (AP) — Stephen Graham dives into the mind of a serial killer for his role in the new Apple TV series “Nocturne.” He binged on true crime documentaries, handpicked by his wife, to prepare for the role. The series is based on Lars Kepler novels. It premieres Friday. It follows a kidnapped teen who resurfaces after three years, while his sister remains missing. Graham plays Jurek Walter, an imprisoned murderer who manipulates those around him. The show features a retired detective, played by Liev Schreiber, and an undercover FBI agent, portrayed by Zazie Beetz. The creators aim to offer a fresh take on the genre.
